title: Wide field image of the Jewel Box
caption: The open cluster NGC 4755, known as the Jewel Box, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope at La Silla
celestial: NGC 4755 · constellation Crux · about 6500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: The star cluster NGC 4755, widely known as the Jewel Box, sits among rich, multicoloured surroundings in this wide view from ESO's La Silla Observatory. The picture comes from the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope and spans 20 arcminutes of sky.

NGC 4755 is an open cluster lying about 6500 light-years away in the direction of Crux. Open clusters are groups of stars born together from the same cloud of gas and dust. Because their members share a common age, they help astronomers compare how stars of different masses develop.

Stars shine in different colours because their surfaces have different temperatures: hotter stars look bluer, cooler ones redder. A wide field like this one places the cluster in context, showing its rich surroundings as well as the cluster itself.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (20.35 x 20.35 arcminutes) and distance (6500 light years), the frame spans roughly 38 × 38 light-years. Its light set out about 6,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image from the Wide Field Imager combines B, V and I filters, from visible light into the near-infrared. The colour assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The I-band light is near-infrared and invisible to the eye, and the long exposures bring out far fainter stars than the eye could see.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture is based on images taken through B, V and I filters, covering visible light and the near-infrared. Its wide field shows the cluster together with its surroundings rather than in isolation.
alt: A star cluster surrounded by a rich, multicoloured field of stars.
